step1_figure.circuit_type: Switched-Capacitor Sample-and-Hold using Fully Differential Two-Stage Op-Amp with SC CMFB
step1_figure.description: The netlist implements the complete switched-capacitor sample-and-hold circuit shown in Fig. 26.58, which incorporates the first-stage diff-amp with SC CMFB (Fig. 26.54), the second-stage output buffer with SC CMFB (Fig. 26.56), the bias generator (Fig. 26.52 / Fig. 26.3), and switched-capacitor common-mode feedback networks (Fig. 26.50).

unity_gain_frequency.description: Unity-gain frequency of the op-amp determined by first-stage transconductance and Miller compensation capacitance

equation.explanation: Calculates the gain-bandwidth / unity-gain frequency of the two-stage operational amplifier based on the input differential pair transconductance gm and compensation capacitor Cc.
equation.assumptions: Diff-pair operates in saturation with Cc = 50 fF and nominal bias current.

sky130_expected.calculation: With Ibias ≈ 20 uA per side, (W/L)_diff = 10/1 (W=1.5 um, L=0.15 um), un*Cox = 270 uA/V^2: gm = sqrt(2 * un*Cox * (W/L) * ID) = sqrt(2 * 270e-6 * 10 * 20e-6) = 328.6 uS. With Cc = 50 fF: fun = 328.6e-6 / (2 * pi * 50e-15) = 1.046 GHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Varies with bias current variation and parasitic capacitance at the first-stage output node.

settling_time.description: Transient settling time of the op-amp outputs to within 1% during the hold/follower phase (phi2 high)

source.reference: Text discussion on settling time (< 3 ns optimized, ~10 ns unoptimized) and Fig. 26.59(b)/26.60(b)

equation.explanation: Time taken from clock edge phi2 going high until the differential output voltage settles to within 1% of its final held value.
equation.assumptions: Closed-loop unity feedback follower during phi2 high with 250 fF load.

sky130_expected.calculation: In unoptimized condition, ts ≈ 10 ns; when sized with wider output buffer and smaller Cc, ts < 3 ns. For nominal 50 fF compensation and standard sizing, ts is roughly 3 ns to 10 ns.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Depends on loop gain, phase margin, and current drive capability of the second-stage buffer.

output_common_mode_voltage.description: Quiescent common-mode voltage of the op-amp differential output buffer

source.reference: Fig. 26.57: Vop = Vom = VCMFB = (ideally) VCM = VDD/2

equation.explanation: The output common-mode voltage established by the switched-capacitor CMFB loop X_X2.
equation.assumptions: Settled CMFB state; ideal reference VCM = 0.5 V (or VDD/2).

sky130_expected.calculation: Set by reference VCM = 0.5 V (or 0.9 V if VDD=1.8V); with netlist reference source VCM = 0.5V, Vocm should settle to 0.50 V.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Determined by SC CMFB switched network charging to the VCM rail.

diff_amp_output_common_mode_voltage.description: Common-mode output voltage of the first-stage diff-amp set by the first-stage CMFB

equation.explanation: The average voltage at the diff-amp outputs vomd and vopd, regulated to Vbias1 to properly bias the PMOS inputs of the output buffer.
equation.assumptions: First stage SC CMFB loop closed during steady-state operation.

sky130_expected.calculation: Vbias1 is generated by diode-connected PMOS in bias circuit; with VDD=1.8V and PMOS |Vth| ≈ 0.42V, Vbias1 is approximately VDD - |Vgs_p| ≈ 1.8 - 0.65 = 1.15 V (or ~0.6V in 1V system). In 1.8V Sky130, Vbias1 ≈ 1.1 to 1.3 V.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Regulated by SC CMFB circuit referencing ideal Vbias1.

diff_amp_tail_voltage_margin.description: Drain voltage of the first-stage NMOS tail current source

source.reference: Page 903: V_tail = VCM - VGS, diff-amp tail source saturation margin

equation.explanation: Voltage dropped across the NMOS tail current sources; must exceed Vds,sat (~100 mV) to maintain saturation.
equation.assumptions: Inputs held at VCM = 0.5 V with NMOS Vth = 0.42 V.

sky130_expected.calculation: With VCM = 0.5 V and VGS ≈ Vth + Von = 0.42 V + 0.06 V = 0.48 V, V_tail = 0.5 - 0.48 = 0.02 V to 0.08 V.
sky130_expected.reasoning: As explained on page 903, with VCM = 500 mV and VGS ~ 400-480 mV, only tens of mV remain across the tail current source unless diff-pair width is widened.

differential_output_voltage_swing.description: Peak-to-peak differential output voltage tracking the differential input signal

equation.explanation: Peak-to-peak differential output amplitude held on C5/C6 during follower/hold phase.
equation.assumptions: 10 MHz sampling clock, 500 kHz sinusoidal input of 0.6 V peak-to-peak differential.

sky130_expected.calculation: The input signal has amplitude 0.3V on each side, so differential peak-to-peak amplitude is 2 * 0.6V = 1.2V peak-to-peak (-0.6V to +0.6V).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Sample-and-hold circuit has unity gain in hold/follower phase, tracking full 1.2 Vpp differential swing.

power_dissipation.description: Total quiescent and active power dissipation of the op-amp and bias network

source.reference: Page 898: Power dissipation discussion; bias circuit sharing

equation.explanation: Average power drawn from the 1.8 V power supply.
equation.assumptions: VDD = 1.8 V, continuous clocking at 10 MHz.

sky130_expected.calculation: Bias network consumes ~40 uA, first stage diff-amp draws ~40 uA, second stage output buffer draws ~80 uA. Total current ≈ 160 uA. P = 1.8 V * 160 uA ≈ 288 uW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Includes static bias branches, dynamic switching of SC CMFB capacitors, and load charging.

step3_testbench.description: Transient simulation testbench of the switched-capacitor sample-and-hold op-amp from Fig. 26.58, measuring unity-gain settling time, common-mode voltages, output swing, and power consumption.
